questions.question: You move a virtual machine and its dependent resources from RG1 to RG2 in the same subscription. Which two statements are true after the move? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: The resource IDs of the moved resources change
options.why: Correct. The resource group name is part of the resource ID.

options.text: The resources remain in the same Azure region
options.why: Correct. Moving between resource groups does not change the region.

options.text: The resources are moved to the region of RG2
options.why: The location of RG2 stores metadata only and does not move resources.

options.text: Role assignments on the virtual machine move with it
options.why: Role assignments made directly on a moved resource are not moved.

questions.explanation: To change region, use Azure Resource Mover or redeploy.

questions.question: You need to move a virtual machine named VM1 from RG1 to RG2. VM1 has an OS disk and a network interface. What should you include in the move?

options.text: VM1, its OS disk and its network interface
options.why: Correct. A virtual machine must move together with its disks and network interfaces.

options.text: VM1 only
options.why: Validation fails when dependent resources are omitted.

options.text: VM1 and the entire virtual network, but not the disk
options.why: The disk must move with the VM.

options.text: Only the OS disk, then re-create VM1 in RG2
options.why: This is not a move operation.

questions.explanation: Across subscriptions, the virtual network must also be moved.

questions.question: Your company creates new subscriptions regularly. Every new subscription must automatically receive the same Azure Policy assignments and role assignments with minimal effort. What should you use?

options.text: A management group that contains the subscriptions, with the assignments made at the management group
options.why: Correct. Child subscriptions inherit assignments from the management group.

options.text: A resource group in each subscription
options.why: Resource groups are below subscriptions and cannot apply settings upward.

options.text: Tags on each subscription
options.why: Tags do not apply policies or roles.

options.text: A separate Microsoft Entra tenant for each subscription
options.why: Separate tenants increase administration and break shared governance.

questions.explanation: You can also set a default management group so new subscriptions are placed under it automatically.

questions.question: What is the maximum depth of a management group hierarchy, excluding the root level and the subscription level?

options.text: Six levels
options.why: Correct. The hierarchy supports up to six levels of depth below the root.

options.text: Three levels
options.why: More levels are supported.

options.text: Ten levels
options.why: The limit is six levels.

options.text: Unlimited
options.why: Depth is limited.

questions.explanation: Each management group and subscription can have only one parent.

questions.question: You need to move a subscription named Sub1 under a management group named MG-NonProd by using Azure CLI. Which command should you run?

options.text: az account management-group subscription add --name MG-NonProd --subscription Sub1
options.why: Correct. This command places the subscription under the management group.

options.text: az account set --subscription MG-NonProd
options.why: This changes the active subscription context.

options.text: az resource move --destination-group MG-NonProd --ids Sub1
options.why: az resource move moves resources between resource groups or subscriptions.

options.text: az group create --name MG-NonProd
options.why: This creates a resource group.

questions.explanation: Moving a subscription requires write permissions on the subscription and on the source and target management groups.
